caption:
A cotton farmer spent five years quietly switching her whole farm away from chemicals. In 2026, the textile industry gave her its top sustainability honour.

Priti Shreedhar Dombe, a cotton farmer from Parbhani district, Maharashtra, spent five years transforming her farming practice - moving from chemical to biological inputs, conserving water and rebuilding the soil health her land had lost. In 2026, she received the Sustainability Champion Award at the Women in Sustainable Cotton Awards, presented at Bharat Tex 2026 in New Delhi by the Better Cotton Initiative and the Confederation of Indian Textile Industry, tied to the UN's International Year of the Woman Farmer. Organizers called her work "a blueprint for what regenerative and climate-resilient agriculture can look like." No shortcuts, no single breakthrough moment - five years of the same quiet work, until the whole industry noticed.
